nodes.summary: FACILITY LOCATION is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a facility location instance that is well-formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The FACILITY LOCATION decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $(o, D, B)$ be a facility location instance with opening costs $o = (o_0, \dots, o_{n-1})$, assignment-cost rows $D = (D_0, \dots, D_{m-1})$ and budget $B$, and write $D_{c,j}$ for the $j$-th entry of the row $D_c$, read as $0$ when $D_c$ has no $j$-th entry. The instance is feasible when there is a map $\sigma$ from the clients $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ to the facilities $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that the opening…
nodes.title: Feasible facility location instances

nodes.summary: A facility location instance is a triple $(o, D, B)$ made of a finite list $o$ of natural numbers (the opening costs of the facilities), a finite list $D$ of finite lists of natural numbers (the $c$-th list holds the costs of assigning client $c$ to each facility), and a natural number $B$ (the budget).
nodes.title: Facility location instances

nodes.summary: FACILITY LOCATION belongs to NP, and every decision problem $L$ in NP reduces to FACILITY LOCATION by a polynomial-time many-one reduction: there is a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bitstrings such that, for every bitstring $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when FACILITY LOCATION accepts $f(x)$.
nodes.title: FACILITY LOCATION is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A facility location instance $(o, D, B)$, with opening costs $o$ and assignment-cost rows $D$, is well-formed when every row of $D$ has the same length as $o$.
nodes.title: Well-formed facility location instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
